texts.facts: The accused u/s 313 Cr.P.C examined on 12.12.2025. The accused Dharmender stated that he was riding a bicycle at Karawal Nagar Labour Chowk at around 9.00 a.m. on the day of incident, which accidentally hit IO/ASI Ravinder Dutt, so he falsely implicated him in the present case. He also verbally and physically abused him. It is stated by other accused persons that accused Dharmender was riding a bicycle at Karawal Nagar Labour Chowk at around 9.00 a.m. on the day of incident, which accidentally hit IO/ASI Ravinder Dutt, so he falsely implicated us in the present case. They also verbally and physically abused Dharmender when they tried to rescue Dharmender. They were also implicated in the present case. No defence evidence was led by the accused despite granting him an opportunity. FINAL ARGUMENTS 05. The court heard final arguments on behalf of the both the parties on 10.02.2026. Ld. Counsel for the accused persons submitted that the case against the accused persons is false and frivolous and has prayed that accused persons be acquitted of the offence charged. PW7 ASI Brijesh Kumar, in his examination in chief deposed that on 12.01.2006, at about 11.30 a.m., ASI Ravinder alongwith other special staff members came at their beat and told him and HC Rajender to join the investigation with them in a case of theft of gas from cylinder and accordingly, they joined the investigation and reached at Khasra No. 94, Industrial Area, where they saw that 6 persons were transmitting the gas from cylinders to another cylinders by using the pipes in a room. He deposed that one person namely Dharmendra alongwith Savan were taking out gas from some cylinders into another cylinder and four other persons namely Joginder, Rajesh, Keshav and Devpal were measuring the weight of the gas cylinders. He deposed that IO SI Rakesh measured the weight of the cylinders and found that the gas which was filled in the each cylinder was less in weight as per the standard rules. He deposed that those cylinders were of Indane brand. 16:16:18 +0800 23. During cross-examination by Ld. Defence Counsel, PW7 testified that he did mark his departure entry personally. He testified that he met three- four special police staff at the spot and he along with other two staff member reached at the spot. He testified that he had not seen the vehicle of the special police staff at the spot and they all were in civil dress. He testified that he remained at the spot for two hours and they all left the spot at different-different times. He testified that the owner of the premises was not called at that point of time. He admitted that the spot was situated at a irregular colony consisted industrial as well as residential area. He testified that he had not met the owner of the Gas Cylinder company ever. He further testified that the statement of the witnesses were recorded at the spot. He testified that the photographs of the cylinders were got clicked at the State vs Sarwan on 10 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36678158/ 9 spot and the photographer was called from the beat staff. He could not say anything about the board which was appearing at the background of the gas cylinders. It admitted that the seizure memo of the said photographs was not prepared and therefore, the same are not attached with the judicial file. 24. He testified that on 02.01.2007, he visited the Shikhawat Gas Agency and seized the stock register. texts.arguments: It is apt to quote the following sections : Section 408 IPC:- "Whoever, being a clerk or servant or employed as a clerk or servant, and being in any manner entrusted in such capacity with property, or with any dominion over property, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine." Section 285 IPC:- "Whoever does, with fire or any combustible matter, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any fire or any combustible matter in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such fire or combustible matter, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both." Section 336 IPC:- "Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may FIR No. 535/2006 State Vs. Sarvan ISRA by ISRA ZAIDI ZAIDI 2026.02.10 16:15:14 +0800 extend to two hundred and fifty rupees, or with both." Section 7 E.C:- "If any person contravenes any order made under section 3, --(a)he shall be punishable,--(i)in the case of an order made with reference to clause (h) or clause (i) of sub-section (2) of that section, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and shall also be liable to fine, and(ii)in the case of any State vs Sarwan on 10 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36678158/ 4 other order, with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine:Provided that the court may, for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment, impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term of less than three months;(b)any property in respect of which the order has been contravened shall be forfeited to the Government;(c)any package, covering or receptacle in which the property is found and any animal, vehicle, vessel or other conveyance used in carrying the commodity shall, if the court so orders, be forfeited to the Government." 07. In the case of Lallu Manjhi and Anr. v. State of Jharkhand (2003) 2 SCC 401 the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India had classified oral State vs Sarwan on 10 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36678158/ 33. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi while dealing with the identity of the Digitally signed by FIR No. 535/2006 State Vs. Sarvan ISRA ISRA ZAIDI ZAIDI 2026.02.10 16:16:44 +0800 accused in the case of Ashraf vs State held as under:- "....However, in case a witness is completely hostile with regard to identity of the accused even in his examination- in-chief and nothing could be elicited from him to show the involvement of the accused in the offence in the cross-exam- ination by the APP, such a testimony cannot be accepted and made the basis of the conviction....." In case of Pradeep Narayan State of Maharashtra AIR 1995 SC 1930 held that failure of police to join witness from locality during search creates doubt about fairness of investigation, benefit of which must go to the accused. In the case of Prem Singh Yadav Vs. CBI 178 (2011) DLT 529 it was held that where it is possible to have both views one in favor of prosecution and one in favor of Digitally signed by FIR No. 535/2006 State Vs. Sarvan ISRA ISRA ZAIDI ZAIDI 2026.02.10 16:17:05 +0800 accused, the later one should prevail. The prosecution could not prove by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt. In a criminal case the burden of proof is on the prosecution to prove the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. The burden never shifts.
